Novohrad Volynskyy Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zhytomyrska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Novohrad-Volyns'kyy — known in Yiddish as Zwiahel or Zvhil — became a major Hasidic center, giving its name to the Zvhil dynasty of rebbes, and by 1897 its Jewish community, a majority of the town at 55 percent, supported one synagogue, 23 separate prayer houses, a hospital, a yeshivah, and a library. Civil War violence in 1919 killed about 1,000 Jews and burned the entire city to the ground; Soviet authorities later closed Jewish religious institutions and demolished this cemetery even before WWII, whose German occupation then brought a ghetto and the murder of over 3,000 people in 1941. The source's own dating for the cemetery is inconsistent — variously placing its founding in the late 17th or mid-18th century and its destruction anywhere from the 1920s through the 1950s — but its site is now overbuilt with private houses; only one illegible matzevah survives, alongside an ohel over the grave of R. Moshe of Zvhil that was demolished around 1950 and rebuilt in 2011.
